evals.name: happy-path-post-apply
evals.prompt: I just applied the checkout unit in myapp-prod. Did it actually deploy?
evals.expected_output: Reads cub unit get + cub unit bridgestate first (confirms LiveRevisionNum advanced, no action error, no gates), then — if the Target is Argo-backed — argocd app get (synced + healthy) and argocd app diff (empty), then kubectl get deploy + describe + pod status. Reports end-to-end in plain English. Does not mutate anything. Offers --web review links.

evals.name: broken-at-cluster
evals.prompt: The apply returned success but the old pods are still running. Something's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Still starts ConfigHub-side (bridge state, revision numbers) to confirm the apply did progress. Then checks controller + cluster, identifying the specific failure mode (ImagePullBackOff / CrashLoopBackOff / OOM / failed probes) via kubectl describe and kubectl logs. Reports the broken link in plain English, pointing at kubectl evidence, and stops without mutating. Suggests cub-mutate or cub-apply --revision LastAppliedRevisionNum (rollback) as next steps, doesn't run them.

evals.name: bulk-post-apply-triage
evals.prompt: We just applied all the staging units and most of them look okay, but I want to know if any didn't finish.
evals.expected_output: Uses cub unit list --space myapp-staging --filter platform/apply-not-completed to surface Units where LastAppliedRevisionNum != LiveRevisionNum, lists them with last action error/time, and for each one drills briefly into controller + cluster to name the broken link. Produces a compact summary rather than dumping everything. Does not mutate.
